The two changed files are pure output artifacts from a benchmark run:

- `benchmarks/results/perf-sf10.html` — a self-contained static HTML dashboard. The only JavaScript is a `toggleTheme()` function that flips a `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`; there's no dynamic data flow, no `innerHTML`/`eval`, no fetch, no user input at runtime. All interpolated values (query IDs, versions, commit SHA, numeric metrics) are baked in at generation time and rendered as static text/SVG/`<title>` tooltips.
- `benchmarks/results/perf-sf10.json` — pure numeric/string data (metadata, latency samples, assertions). No code, no schema references executable.

Neither file is imported or read by anything else in the repo (no references found). The generator (`benchmarks.dashboard.generate`) is not part of this diff, so any escaping/serialization concerns would belong to a future review of that generator, not this artifact-only change. No entry points, sinks, or attacker-influenceable flows exist within the touched files.
